## Observed Facts

- **Count:** 20,217 BGL Log Entries have "ciod" in the message between 2005-06-01 and 2005-07-01 (end exclusive) [E1]. The match is a case-insensitive substring on `message`. By component: APP 13,409, KERNEL 6,803, MMCS 5 [E1].
- **First matching entry:** line 4988, 2005-06-03 16:17:40.190183, node R26-M0-NC-I:J18-U11, component APP, level FATAL: `ciod: Error loading /p/gb2/stella/RAPTOR/65641/raptor: invalid or missing program image, No such file or directory` [E2][E3].
- **Just before (lines 4980–4987):** Eight KERNEL INFO entries from 16:12:35 to 16:16:26 on other nodes (R16-M1-N2-C, R22-M0-NB/N9/NF-C). They are ECC-style lines ("CE sym 2 … mask …", "total of 31 ddr error(s) detected and corrected") followed by four "generating core.N" lines (cores 257, 385, 65, 1) [E3].
- **Just after (lines 4989–4996):** The same FATAL `ciod: Error loading … raptor` message repeats on about one node every 20–40 ms, across R26-M0 (NC, N8, N4, N0 on J18) and then R27-M1-NC-I:J18-U11 at 16:17:40.445858 [E3]. This is a burst of identical errors, not a single failure.

## Hypotheses

- The ciod failures look like a job launch problem: the control daemon could not find the program image `/p/gb2/stella/RAPTOR/65641/raptor` on the I/O nodes. "No such file or directory" points to a missing or unmounted path, or a binary that was moved or never staged.
- The KERNEL core-dump lines just before the burst may be unrelated. They come from different nodes and do not name the same job. Treat them as a possible earlier event, not the cause.

## Unknowns

- The logs do not show whether the RAPTOR binary was missing from the filesystem or whether the path was unreachable (for example, a mount failure). The message alone does not settle this.
- The logs do not name the job or user that submitted the run, so I cannot link the core dumps to the failed load.
- I did not check whether the 20,217 matches are mostly this same error. I only sampled the first entries.

## Next Step

Run a count of the exact error text in the same window, grouped by node, to see how many I/O nodes hit it:
`count_by(dataset=BGL, group_by=node, query="Error loading /p/gb2/stella/RAPTOR/65641/raptor", start=2005-06-01, end=2005-07-01)`.
Then search for other entries mentioning `/p/gb2/stella` or `RAPTOR` near 2005-06-03 16:17 to see whether the path or the file was changed around that time.
